record.paper_title: Understanding Solar Flares and Energetic Events: Open questions, observational requirements, and instrumental needs over the coming decade
record.original_question: To what extent does solar-flare physics scale continuously from the largest stellar and solar superflares through X-class events down to microflares, nanoflares, and campfires, and what similarities or differences in reconnection, particle acceleration, and plasma heating emerge across that full range of event sizes?

evidence.quote: 6. How does the physics of ﬂares scale from superﬂares, to X-class events down to nanoﬂares?

An open question is, to what extent does the physics of ﬂares scale from the very big to the very small? What are the key similarities and differences in the reconnection, particle acceleration, and plasma heating that results?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Solar and stellar flares are impulsive releases of magnetic energy in a plasma atmosphere, driven by magnetic reconnection and accompanied by particle acceleration and plasma heating. Observed events span an enormous energy range, conventionally classified (in approximate order of decreasing radiative energy) as: stellar superflares and solar superflares (≳10^33 erg), X-class flares (≳10^32 erg in soft X-rays at GOES X1 level), through M-, C-, B-, and A-class flares, microflares (≈10^26–10^28 erg), nanoflares (≈10^24 erg, as hypothesized by Parker for coronal heating), and the small ubiquitous EUV brightenings known as campfires (≈10^22–10^24 erg).

Formulate and resolve the following question. Let E denote the total released magnetic/radiative energy of a flare-like event. Consider the key physical observables and parameters associated with each event:

• reconnection rate M_A (the inflow Alfvén Mach number at the reconnection region) and reconnected magnetic flux Φ_rec;
• nonthermal particle acceleration efficiency, characterized by the fraction η_nt of E going into accelerated electrons and ions, the power-law index δ of the accelerated electron spectrum, and the cutoff energies;
• plasma heating, characterized by the peak temperature T_peak, the emission measure EM, and the partition between direct heating and chromospheric evaporation driven by accelerated particles.

The problem is: determine, on the basis of magnetohydrodynamic and kinetic plasma physics, whether there exist universal scaling laws of the form

  T_peak ∝ E^{a}, EM ∝ E^{b}, Φ_rec ∝ E^{c}, η_nt ∝ E^{d}, δ = δ(E), M_A = M_A(E)

that hold continuously across the full range from campfires (E ∼ 10^22 erg) to stellar superflares (E ∼ 10^36 erg), and identify which scaling relations (if any) extend uniformly across this ≳14-decade range in energy, and where, if anywhere, qualitative breaks occur (for instance, transitions in the dominant reconnection regime, in the efficiency or spectral hardness of particle acceleration, or in the relative role of direct versus evaporative heating). Specifically, characterize the similarities and differences in reconnection geometry and rate, in particle-acceleration mechanisms (e.g., DC electric field, stochastic, shock, or termination-shock acceleration), and in chromospheric/coronal heating responses, as a function of E across this range.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an explicitly stated open question in current solar/stellar flare physics. Reviews and recent surveys describe partial scaling relations (e.g., Shibata–Yokoyama temperature–emission-measure scaling, Aschwanden's flare statistics, stellar superflare studies with Kepler/TESS) but no unified theory verified across the full range from campfires to superflares; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Shibata & Yokoyama scaling law for solar and stellar flares
status_evidence.snippet: A unified scaling law relating flare temperature, emission measure, and magnetic field is proposed and compared with solar and stellar flares.
status_evidence.claim: Partial scaling relations exist between solar and stellar flares but do not constitute a complete cross-scale theory.

status_evidence.title: Solar Orbiter discovery of 'campfires' (Berghmans et al. 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Small-scale EUV brightenings ('campfires') are observed but their relation to nanoflare heating and larger flares remains under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The continuity of physics from campfires up to large flares is an active, unresolved research question.

status_evidence.title: Stellar superflares on solar-type stars (Maehara et al., Notsu et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Superflare statistics on solar-type stars suggest similarities to solar flare scaling but with open questions about whether the same magnetic reconnection physics applies.
status_evidence.claim: Whether superflare physics scales continuously to solar/microflare regimes is unresolved.
